verses.1: They then traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, and arrived in Thessaloniki, where the Jews were gathered together.
verses.2: But according to the instructions of Paul, he came to them and on Saturday he selected three men from among them to read those writings to them.
verses.3: I also believe that Christ should suffer and rise from the dead. And this person is indeed Christ, Jesus, whom I declare to you today.
verses.4: And some of them were also summoned and brought before Paul and Silas. They were among a large number of women who respected the Greek Church; not a few of them were among the first women to follow Christ.
verses.5: As the Jews grew richer, they hired some wicked men to lead the crowd. They caused chaos in the city. When they arrived at Jason’s house, they tried to get him to bring them into the city.
verses.6: But they couldn’t find any people who could arrest them. They tried to get Yasona and some of his brothers to help them, hoping that those who were causing trouble in their city would be taken away from there as well.
verses.7: Just as James is understood in this way; and all of them reject the teachings of the Emperor. They claim that Jesus is another king.
verses.8: But they also disturbed the crowd and the city commanders when they heard this.
verses.9: And after receiving what was due from Iason, they dismissed them along with the others.
verses.10: And the brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas to Berea, because they wanted to join the Jews there.
verses.11: These people were more noble than those in Thessaloniki. They listened to the arguments with great enthusiasm, and every day they would check whether what was written was indeed true.
verses.12: Many of them believed in this, and not a few among the Greek women and men also believed in it.
verses.13: But when the Jews from Thessaloniki heard that Paul also was accused in Berea for his teachings about God, they went there to provoke and annoy the people there.
verses.14: At that time, the brothers immediately sent Paul on his way until he reached the sea. Silas and Timothy also stayed there.
verses.15: And those who placed Paul in custody brought him to Athens. They received orders from Silanus and Timotheus to come to him as quickly as possible.
verses.16: And in Athens, where they were received by Paul, his spirit continued to guide them as they observed the appearance of the city.
verses.17: So, disputes were resolved within the community of Jews, as well as among those who respected each other. These disputes were also addressed in the marketplace every day, by those who were willing to settle them.
verses.18: And even some of the Ephesians and Stoics who were philosophers joined in with him. Some said, “What does this prophet say?” Others replied, “It seems that those who accuse Jesus and His resurrection are demons.”
verses.19: They also took him to Mount Aréion, saying, “Let us know who this new teacher is who is giving these teachings.”
verses.20: We would like to hear some suggestions regarding these matters. We hope to know what these things should be.
verses.21: All the Athenians, as well as those foreigners who settled there, did nothing else but talk about something new or hear something new.
verses.22: Standing still on the middle of the sacred mountain, Paul said, “Men of Athens, I consider you to be utterly insane.”
verses.23: For I have also found your offerings and sacrifices, which were offered there. They were recorded as belonging to the god Agnostus. Now, since you do not know this, I declare this to you.
verses.24: The God who created the world and everything within it; this Lord of heaven and earth does not dwell in any human-made temples.
verses.25: Nor is it treated by human hands. It gives life, breath, and everything else to those who receive it.
verses.26: And he created all those people who live on every side of the earth. He also considered the various times and conditions necessary for their settlement there.
verses.27: We should seek the Lord, if only so that He might bless him and protect him. After all, this is something that exists between each of us from time to time.
verses.28: For in him we live, we move, and we are born again. This is what some of the poets who wrote about you have said. For it is from him that our lineage comes.
verses.29: Therefore, since there exist creatures that belong to God, we should not consider them to be mere gold, silver, or stones. They are, rather, symbols of human craftsmanship and inspiration; they represent something divine.
verses.30: Therefore, after those who have lived in ignorance for so long, God now commands all people to repent completely.
verses.31: Since he spent a day in hell, where he was to be judged fairly by a man who had the power to judge others. He was given faith, and he rose from the dead.
verses.32: When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some laughed; others said, “Hear what you have to say again.”
verses.33: In this way, Paul came out from among them.
verses.34: Some men, however, believed in him. Among them were Dionysus the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others along with them.
